name: Photronics, Inc.
reason: Commodity-like photomask supplier in the semiconductor capex cycle with adjusted EPS at 0.98x its 10y max and EBIT margin 24.5% vs a 10y avg of 16.5% after a 2022 step-up, 10y ROIC only 7.8% and consensus EPS growth of 0-7%; no durable route to >=7% growth from a cyclical high.

name: Ultra Clean Holdings, Inc.
reason: Low-margin semiconductor-equipment subsystem supplier (EBIT margin 2.1%, 10y avg 5.4%, 10y ROIC 4.4%) whose earnings swing with WFE spending (EPS -86% in 2023), with acquisitions at 1.9x cumulative FCF, shares up 3.7%/yr and adjusted EPS far above GAAP; ordinary and unforecastable.

name: EOG Resources, Inc.
reason: Best-in-class oil and gas E&P with a strong balance sheet (net debt/EBITDA 0.49x), but earnings are set by crude and gas prices (EPS swung from -1.61 in 2016 to 13.76 in 2022) and consensus sees FY2-FY3 EPS declines; fails the commodity-price test.

name: Brunswick Corporation
reason: Discretionary recreational marine maker whose adjusted EPS fell from 10.03 (2022) to 3.27 (0.33x 10y max) with margin in the 9th percentile, net debt/EBITDA 3.26x for a highly cyclical business and acquisitions at 0.88x FCF; cyclical with leverage, no specialness.

name: Dycom Industries, Inc.
reason: Telecom/fiber and data-center contractor riding a real broadband/AI build-out, but EPS is at 1.0x its 10y max with margin in the 91st percentile, revenue depends on a handful of large carriers, acquisitions run 1.9x cumulative FCF and net debt/EBITDA is 3.2x; history shows boom-bust (EPS -47% in 2018, 2.6% margin in 2021).

name: First Merchants Corp
reason: Ordinary Indiana commercial bank with 10y ROE of 9.9%, share count up 4.2%/yr from acquisitions and EPS at 1.0x its 10y peak on a rate tailwind; consensus FY1 EPS -17%; no low-cost-deposit or underwriting edge that makes it special.

name: UFP Industries, Inc.
reason: Well-run, net-cash (net debt/EBITDA -1.1x) wood products converter with 10y ROIC 14.8%, but earnings are driven by lumber prices and housing/R&R volumes (EPS 3.99 to 10.99 to 5.01 over 2020-25, now 0.46x peak) so 5-10y earnings cannot be forecast with confidence.

name: Beacon Financial Corporation
reason: Newly formed (Sept 2025) merger of Brookline Bancorp and Berkshire Hills with 10y ROE of 2.5%, adjusted EPS lower than 2015 (-2.5%/yr CAGR), share count up 11.9%/yr and a large adj-vs-GAAP gap; acquisition-driven, low-return bank in mid-integration.

name: Carlisle Companies Incorporated
reason: Leading share in a consolidated US commercial single-ply roofing market where ~70% of demand is non-discretionary re-roofing, now a focused building-envelope pure play with 20.4% EBIT margin, 1.18x FCF conversion, net debt/EBITDA 1.56x and shares down 4.1%/yr via buybacks (0.95x FCF), compounding adjusted EPS 14.9%/yr; caveats are EPS at 0.96x peak with margin in the 82nd percentile and soft new-construction demand.

name: PPG Industries, Inc.
reason: Large coatings franchise but revenue grew 0.3%/yr and adjusted EPS only 2.9%/yr over 10 years (2/10 years >=7%), with auto OEM/industrial cyclicality, raw-material pass-through and a 27.5% adj-vs-GAAP gap; good but ordinary with no route to >=7% growth.

name: Trustmark Corporation
reason: Conservative Mississippi regional bank but with 10y ROE of 7.9%, EPS at 1.0x its 10y high on rate tailwinds and a 2025 insurance sale, and consensus FY2-FY3 growth of 5-9%; cheap-but-ordinary with no specialness.

name: Zimmer Biomet Holdings, Inc.
reason: Orthopedic reconstruction oligopolist but adjusted EPS grew only 2.1%/yr over 10y with revenue 3.2%/yr, 10y ROIC 3.2% after the Biomet deal, adjusted EPS roughly 3x GAAP, net debt/EBITDA 2.96x and persistent share loss to Stryker in robotics; consensus LTG 4.4%.

name: BorgWarner Inc.
reason: Auto-parts supplier whose core turbo/drivetrain products face a credible EV-transition threat within 5 years while its EV bets have been written down (adjusted EPS roughly 2x GAAP), 10y ROIC 6.9% and EPS at 1.0x its 10y max in a cyclical industry.

name: MGIC Investment Corporation
reason: Mortgage insurer whose earnings depend on the housing credit cycle (EPS -67% in 2016, near-wipeout in 2008-10) and are at 1.0x the 10y max on exceptionally benign loss reserves, with consensus EPS growth of only 2-5%; buybacks (shares -6.7%/yr) cannot offset cycle risk.

name: Prosperity Bancshares, Inc.(R)
reason: Conservatively underwritten Texas bank with a low-cost deposit base, but adjusted EPS grew only 3.4%/yr over 10y (0.1%/yr over 5y) with shares up 3.1%/yr from acquisitions and 10y ROE of 7.5%; disciplined but no route to >=7% organic EPS growth.

name: First Horizon Corporation
reason: Regional bank whose 18.7% EPS CAGR comes off a depressed 2015 base and the IBERIABANK merger (shares up 8.0%/yr), with EPS at 1.0x its 10y max, 10y ROE of 10.3% and a capital-markets/mortgage-sensitive fixed-income unit; ordinary and acquisition-driven.

name: Citigroup Inc.
reason: Global universal bank mid-way through a multi-year restructuring and regulatory consent-order remediation, with 10y ROE of 6.3%, EPS swinging 4.04-10.14 and earnings tied to capital-markets activity and global credit; the turnaround may work but the outcome cannot be forecast with confidence.

name: First Busey Corporation
reason: Midwest bank whose revenue growth (19%/yr) came from acquisitions such as CrossFirst with shares up 11.3%/yr while adjusted EPS fell to 1.29 (-0.2%/yr 10y CAGR, 0.56x 10y max); acquisition-driven with no per-share growth.

name: Bank OZK
reason: Highly efficient bank with 11.5%/yr EPS growth and 11.9% avg ROE, but earnings rest on a concentrated, large-ticket CRE construction book (RESG) funded largely by CDs rather than low-cost deposits, and EPS is at 1.0x its 10y max; a CRE downturn outcome is not forecastable.

name: CBIZ, Inc.
reason: Middle-market accounting/benefits advisor whose growth comes from acquisitions (1.34x cumulative FCF, including the transformational 2024 Marcum deal) with net debt/EBITDA 4.21x, EPS at 1.0x its 10y max with margin in the 91st percentile, a 68% adj-vs-GAAP gap and AI-disintermediation risk to tax/accounting work.
